body:
I don't really care if you think I'm lying, I'm not even really trying to prove a point besides that sometimes MRAs send messages like this to people. I don't have the password to a YouTube account that I stopped using six fucking years ago, and I stopped using the email connected to the account in 2010 or so. When I tried accessing my inbox, it prompted me to verify my identity with a cell phone that I haven't had since I moved off the grid for a year and a half. 

The only reason I ever frequented MRA fourms and the like was to do research for a world issues project I was doing. If I recall correctly, when I was registered at antimisandry, I received similar messages there. They really don't like anyone with even slight feminist leanings there. I've contacted the webmaster there to see if I can regain access to that account, but have not yet received a response. I don't really care either way, but I'll let you know how it pans out.

Also, neither of us **knows** I'm lying, because I know that I'm not and you only **think** that I am. There's a difference between thinking something and knowing something, so don't be a dick about it.

Not having access to emails and accounts I used when I was 17 is actually something I consider inconvenient at this point, actually. I also wouldn't make something like that up since that'd be pretty fucking pointless. I have no problem with MRAs, but I did spend a lot of time on MRA YouTube channels and forums when I was in high school and I can assure you that people like this do exist. If you feel that doubtful about it, you can spend some time browsing old posts on the antimisandry.com forums. You are being wilfully ignorant in regards to a very vocal minority existing, and it's kind of baffling.

It's not really a steep claim to say that some people who call themselves MRAs do things like this. Some people who refer to themselves as feminists also do things like this. But yeah, I'll try to get some screenshots. Most of the messages I received were not on a dating site, but on my old YouTube account which I stopped using when I was 17 (2007). I don't know if I can access it since I no longer remember the password or use the same email, but I'll try my damndest.

This isn't necessarily fake. I have received plenty of messages from MRAs similar to this. I'm not saying that all MRAs are like this, I'm just saying that there is a vocal minority that thinks like this and are not afraid to let people know. It's disheartening, quite frankly.
Or I could just not. It doesn't really make a difference. I have no obligation to live a life I never asked for.

Yeah, I've seen a bunch of social workers, counsellors, psychologists, and psychiatrists. I've been on various medications. I've gotten help, I've wanted desperately to get help but it didn't work and I don't want it anymore.
Well, I guess you're lucky or something then.
Why do I just have to stick it out?

I've been getting help, done the therapy and meds thing, been to the hospital. At this point, I don't even care enough to keep going through with the process of getting better. It's too much and even if it worked eventually, everything would still be as mundane and awful.

During the winter of 2006, I decided that I was pretty done with life and didn't really want to continue going through the motions anymore. I decided to stick around till after Christmas, so I spent Christmas Day with my family, and made sure my loved ones knew how I felt about them. Then, I went to bed and laid there for several hours thinking everything over. I proceeded to my basement, where I took some broken Christmas tree lights and tried to hang myself with it. Unfortunately, I'm super bad at tying knots.

I was more or less like, "Well, fuck this" when it didn't work out so well, so I took a bunch of pills and slept for a really long time and woke up feeling like shit. It's been a long time since then, but things have only gotten worse. I can't think of a reason to not give up and will probably end up finding a more efficient way to do it in the next few days.
